label: Meaning of reduccion
quiz: What did reduccion concern in this lesson?
Concentrating or relocating people into settlements
Creating people with no earlier history
A guaranteed voluntary move by every family
A modern census with exact travel times
retry: What does a relocation instruction establish by itself?
A planned change, not proof of every household's move
Complete implementation everywhere
Everyone's private agreement
A complete record of actual residence
hard: A report says a proposed center proves all residents moved. What is missing?
Evidence of actual residence and local responses
Only a larger label on the plan
An assumption that all plans succeed
A fictional speech of universal approval

label: Aims and effects
quiz: Which statement identifies an administrative aim rather than an observed result?
Officials wanted contact and collection easier to organize
A particular household moved according to a dated record
A later petition requested a change
A building was documented as occupied
retry: Why keep an official aim separate from local consent?
An authority's purpose is not everyone's wishes
All people always wanted what officials wanted
A purpose proves all results
A religious aim shows everyone shared one belief
hard: An account claims a move was beneficial because officials intended easier administration. What is needed?
Evidence of actual effects on affected households
Only a repeated statement of the intention
A claim that intentions guarantee results
An invented family story presented as original

label: Plans and practice
quiz: What does a proposed layout most directly show?
An intended arrangement, not complete evidence of later buildings and residence
Every resident's exact daily journey
Proof all design rules were followed everywhere
Universal agreement to move
retry: Why should a teaching diagram without scale not supply travel minutes?
It lacks the evidence needed for actual distance and travel time
All journeys take identical time
Every path represents a fixed number of minutes
A town name makes every line exact
hard: A settlement rule describes what should be built. Which additional record helps check implementation?
Evidence of what was built and occupied in that place and period
Only another copy of the rule
Only an official's favorable label
An assumption that every prescription was fulfilled

label: Daily life
quiz: What should be included when studying a residence change?
Connections to work, water, relatives and institutions
Only the location of an office
Only the policy name
A universal claim about all families
retry: What can the fictional nearer-office/farther-work example establish?
Different possible relationships, not every historical household's distances
One authentic journey time for every family
Guaranteed improvement in every activity
A complete historical map
hard: A plan shortens one connection but has no work-site evidence. What remains to investigate?
How the actual household maintained work and resources
Why all effects must be positive
Which invented distance applies everywhere
Why local routines no longer matter

label: Local responses
quiz: What does a petition requesting a settlement change establish?
A request was made, not necessarily granted
Everyone supported the same outcome
All households moved willingly
No local person took action
retry: Why compare an official report with residence evidence?
Reported compliance may not establish actual residence or all local experiences
All official records are useless
A title guarantees complete knowledge
A map supplies every person's viewpoint
hard: An order and a request to revise it survive, but no reply does. What is careful?
Identify both actions and state that the outcome needs more evidence
Declare the request successful
Assume no response occurred
Invent a final decision and present it as original
